idea.description: SASRec predicts the next item using causal self-attention over a user's interaction history. Item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting features score candidate items through shared item embeddings. Training uses shifted next-item targets and sampled negatives. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1)
idea.motivation: Attention lets the model emphasize recent actions in sparse histories while using longer-range context when useful. This is relevant to categories with different interaction densities. Despite the supplied title, standard SASRec does not solve cold start for users without histories or items without training interactions. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781)
idea.implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and preserve routing for all four categories. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Select configurations using only the pinned macro validation HR@10. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory and update the predictor writer whenever architecture changes. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), reporting measured metrics with definitions. No task-specific improvement has been measured.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in four_categories:
    load unchanged RecHarness splits
    initialize category SASRec with training seed 42
    for epoch in configured_epochs:
        for _, sequence, positive, negative in train_loader:
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            pos_logits = score(features, positive)
            neg_logits = score(features, negative)
            loss = masked_mean(softplus(-pos_logits) + softplus(neg_logits))
            optimize(loss)
        evaluate through pinned validation protocol
        save eligible checkpoint beneath trial directory
select configuration by macro validation HR@10
write working/predict.py with matching architecture and category routing

originality.positive: The original paper introduced an influential application of self-attention to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: For this task, SASRec is already the prescribed baseline; the supplied idea adds no distinct cold-start mechanism.

future_potential.positive: Category-specific regularization and sequence-length tuning are plausible extensions. Public titles and descriptions could support a separately evaluated cold-start extension.
future_potential.negative: Benefits remain unmeasured, and interaction-only embeddings provide limited support for unseen items.

code_difficulty.positive: The existing baseline and compatibility interface reduce implementation work.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct padding and causal masks, predictor parity, diagnostic compatibility, and budget-aware validation still require care.

report:
Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.
